units.content: Implemented experiment tests Delta G_m != Delta Omega and whether adoption is required between generator improvement and realized phase transition.

content.success: generator improves, adoption succeeds, frontier expands
content.barrier: generator improves, adoption friction blocks frontier
content.resource: no effective adopted generator; frontier grows externally

units.content: 120 steps; initial C=1,P=10,G=1,A=1; alpha=.15,gamma=.15,G_capacity=20,rho_success=.08,rho_barrier=.08,friction=.10,beta=.04,P_capacity=10000.
C tracks P; G grows logistically; A follows G or is friction-reduced; frontier growth depends on adopted generator except resource condition.
Lambda is C-old_C and Omega is change in Lambda, a simulation-specific acceleration proxy rather than validated Omega measurement.
Program prints tables/final values and an interpretation predicting G_m growth in both adaptive cases but Omega/C transition only with successful adoption; no frozen run output is admitted.
Minimal baseline reference implementation separating resource-driven growth from generator-driven acceleration; explicitly says it does not model intelligence.
AdaptiveState stores capability, search capacity, generator capacity, resources and history.
Defaults resource_growth=.05, search_learning=.02, generator_learning=0; direct-run sets generator_learning=.01 and 20 steps.
reachable_space proxy =1+resources*capability*(1+search)*(1+generator); source explicitly says this is not literal possibility-space measurement.
omega_estimate returns generator_capacity as proxy for generator contribution; Lambda is log change of reachable proxy.
Direct run prints per-step capability/resources/search/generator/Lambda/Omega; no execution record is stored.
Tests Delta G_m->Delta Omega->Delta P_reach->Delta C under generator saturation, resource cost and diminishing frontier returns.
Implements fixed-frontier baseline, resource-scaling system and constrained evolutionary generator system.
100 steps; alpha=.15,gamma=.25,G_capacity=100,beta=.03,resource_growth=1.05,generator_cost=.02 and chosen initial conditions.
Evolutionary G grows logistically, expands P multiplicatively, consumes R, and capability tracks P; resource system grows R and adds frontier externally.
Omega stored as G-previous_G in evolutionary system, distinct from other simulation files' acceleration proxy definitions.
Program prints final metrics/crossover and framework interpretation; no stored run outcome establishes that crossover or hypothesis support occurred.
Tests temporal ordering t_Gm<t_Omega<t_C with adoption/activation lag between generator improvement and frontier/capability effects.
Implements baseline, resource-scaling and delayed evolutionary system with G potential and slowly adapting A.
120 steps; alpha=.15,gamma=.12,G_capacity=20,rho=.05,beta=.04,P_capacity=10000 plus fixed initial values.
C tracks frontier; G logistic; A slowly catches G; adopted A drives logistic frontier growth.
t_Gm is first G>initial, t_Omega is maximum Lambda acceleration, t_C is maximum Lambda; Omega=change in capability velocity.
Program prints 'Temporal ordering detected' / 'Evidence is consistent with' only if programmed inequality holds; no frozen execution record makes those observed results.
Frozen Python blob contains exactly one newline and no executable statements, comments, hypotheses, parameters, outputs or results.
Implemented experiment tests source hypothesis that generator improvement is necessary but not sufficient for phase boundary.

content.failure: G improvement + very low adoption rate

units.content: 100 steps; alpha=.15,gamma=.15,G_capacity=20,rho_success=.08,rho_failure=.005,beta=.04,P_capacity=10000.
C tracks P; G grows in all modes; adoption rate differs; adaptive frontier depends on A; resource frontier uses external increment.
Omega=change in capability velocity, not direct generator contribution.
Program prints success/failure/resource metrics and expected framework test narrative; filename/labels do not constitute a reported negative result without execution record.
Models transition from systems improving outputs to systems improving mechanisms producing outputs; isolates improvement of improvement mechanism.
GeneratorState stores capability, search capacity, generator capacity, generator_dynamics and history.
GeneratorAdaptiveSystem defaults generator_learning_rate=.05, meta_learning_rate=0; comparison uses fixed system rates 0/0 and generator system .05/.01.
G_m grows from search; generator_dynamics grows by meta rate times Delta G_m; capability multiplies using search+generator; search grows from generator.
omega() returns generator_dynamics; docstring maps framework Omega=Delta_G to local approximation dG_m/dt.
compare_systems prints ten-step capability trajectories for fixed vs improving generator; no run artifact is stored.
Path is an exact blob-identity occurrence of experiments/simulations/generator_adaptation.py; semantic units are inherited by exact content identity rather than reparsed as independent content.
Compares resource scaling against self-improving generator over long horizon; predicts resource system may win early and generator system eventually cross.
100 steps; resource_growth=1.15 with exponential saturation; generator_growth=1.15; alpha=.05; fixed initial state.
Resource capability multiplies with resources; resources grow then decay/saturate; generator fixed.
Generator capability multiplies using G; G self-multiplies by generator_growth; resources fixed.
Omega stored as generator - previous_generator.
Program searches for first capability crossover and can print 'Evidence consistent with' or 'No phase boundary detected'; no stored run outcome is admitted.
Tests Delta G_m->Delta Omega->Delta C by comparing fixed generator with self-modifying improving generator.
compute_omega forms per-step Delta C/Delta G_m then returns final-minus-first efficiency; zero efficiencies when Delta G_m=0.
fixed_generator starts capability 1.15, generator 1 and multiplies capability 1.15 each step with generator unchanged.
improving_generator starts capability 1.20, generator 1, generator_growth .15; generator and growth rate compound and capability multiplies by generator.
Runs both ten-step scenarios, computes local Omega proxy and compares improving_omega to fixed_omega.
Can print 'Evidence consistent with' and 'higher evolutionary velocity' based entirely on programmed synthetic trajectories; no frozen execution record or empirical standing.
Tests core hypothesis against baseline and resource-scaling alternatives using three synthetic systems.
Resources and generator multiply by configured rates; capability productivity=.05*resources*generator.
omega_proxy=capability_gain*delta_gm, a file-local proxy not the repository's unique Omega definition.
Program comments predict Omega_evolutionary > Omega_resource > Omega_baseline and Delta G_m preceding Delta C.
Program runs systems at import/direct execution and prints phase-boundary analysis plus prediction narrative; repository presence does not prove execution.
Tests stronger Delta G_m->Delta Omega->Delta P_reach->Delta C hypothesis; contrasts fixed frontier resource system with expanding-frontier evolutionary system.
50 steps; alpha=.15,beta=.05,gamma=.10, initial C=1,P=10,G=1.
Resource condition actually keeps P and G fixed while C approaches P; source labels it resource system despite no explicit resource state variable.
C tracks P; P multiplies by 1+beta*G_m; G_m multiplies by 1+gamma.
Omega=G_m-previous_G_m.
Program finds synthetic crossover and prints framework interpretation that evolutionary system creates new reachable possibilities; no frozen run output is reported.
Tests phase-boundary chain under generator saturation, frontier saturation and diminishing resource returns.
100 steps; alpha=.20,gamma=.20,G_capacity=10,beta=.05,P_capacity=1000, resource_growth=1.08, resource_frontier_gain=.05.
Implements fixed baseline, resource frontier expansion with saturation, and evolutionary logistic generator/frontier expansion.
Lambda=C-previous_C and Omega=Lambda-previous_lambda; this differs from generator-difference proxies in other simulation files.
Program searches first evolutionary C > resource C crossover and reports final C/P/G/Lambda/Omega.
Prints expected signature and says a phase boundary exists if trajectory class changes; no stored run record turns this into an observed result.

variants: change in Delta C/Delta G_m efficiency
